title: Mapping Toxic Comments Across Demographics: A Dataset from German Public Broadcasting

bias_targets.methodology: Annotating German social media comments for toxicity targeted at religion and evaluating multiple LLMs' (e.g., GPT-4o, Llama-3) classification performance against human annotations using metrics like Macro F1, MCC, and Cohen's kappa.
Labeling comments for hate speech directed at ethnic, racial, or national identities and assessing the multi-class prediction accuracy and agreement of LLMs versus human consensus.
Identifying toxic language targeting gender and sexual identity in multi-platform social media comments to analyze demographic patterns and evaluate LLM automated detection capabilities.
Classifying text for toxicity based on physical conditions and measuring the zero-shot and fine-tuned performance of language models in detecting these specific targets.
Categorizing toxic speech aimed at socioeconomic classes and evaluating prompt-based classification abilities of models to scale multi-label hate speech annotation.
Annotating comments for occupation-based hate and comparing human inter-annotator agreement with the annotation consistency of several large language models.
